subject: SLA: capacity expectations & credit anchoring
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@kitetek.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@kitetek.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask for Q3 pilot — capacity expectation and credits

Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers look promising for our use case. Before we kick off the Q3 pilot I need to align internally on the SLA baseline and the monthly remedy cap. A couple of asks from our side: 

- Baseline uptime: can we agree to 99.90% for the pilot (we're asking to relax from your standard 99.95% given this is a bursty pilot)?
- Monthly credit cap: we would prefer a hard cap so our procurement team can model worst-case liability. Could Redwood do a cap at 25% of one monthly invoice for the pilot months?
- Mitigations: if you agree to the lower uptime floor, can you commit to an operational playbook (on-call escalation + pre-warm capacity plan) included as an appendix to the SLA?

I attached a short traffic forecast and a marked-up SLA template highlighting the two items above. Our legal & procurement teams are on contracts@kitetek.com — copying them to get a sense on timing.

Can you confirm what Redwood would need to accept this scope and any alternatives if a hard cap isn't feasible?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
Head of Platform Engineering
KiteTek

Attachment: KiteTek_SLA_Markup_v1.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: Q2-traffic-forecast.csv (csv)
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@kitetek.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for Q3 pilot — capacity expectation and credits

Sara — really appreciate the clarity and the forecast. Short answers up front: we can be flexible, but there are tradeoffs.

- Baseline uptime: For a pilot run with bursty traffic and no long-term reserved capacity, our standard is 99.95%. We can provision an interim 99.90% floor for the pilot provided we include a documented mitigation plan (pre-warm and a fallback model variant).
- Monthly credit cap: We typically avoid hard caps on remedy exposure because it weakens the incentive to remediate. That said, for commercial pilots we have offered a capped remedy in negotiated pilots before. I can propose a pilot cap at 20% of the monthly invoice with quarterly review points.
- Mitigations: happy to include the operational playbook. We will provide a pre-warm runbook and a single-point escalation (CS + infra on-call) in the appendix.

If that sounds reasonable I will loop in product and legal (cc'd) and share a redline of the SLA with those numbers. If KiteTek needs a firmer ceiling we can discuss a higher pilot fee that correspondingly lowers remedy exposure.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: SLA ask for Q3 pilot — capacity expectation and credits

Internal — forwarding KiteTek's ask. Key negotiation points and my recommended approach below.

Quote from KiteTek:
- Request temporary baseline of 99.90% (pilot), and hard monthly credit cap at 25% of invoice.

My recommendation:
- Offer 99.90% for pilot with a documented mitigation appendix (pre-warm plan + fallback model variant + escalation matrix). This keeps customer comfortable on availability while protecting our public SLAs.
- Counter on cap: propose 20% cap for pilot months with a clause to revisit after 60 days or on hitting a usage trigger. Explain that the lower cap is tied to an increased pilot fee (one-time provisioning credit) — propose a 10% provisioning fee on the first month to offset remediation risk.
- Legal: we should add a carveout for maintenance windows and for customer-originated traffic spikes outside the agreed forecast. We can use their attached forecast to set a baseline.

Open questions for you both:
1) Is 20% cap + 10% provisioning fee acceptable commercially?
2) Do we have product sign-off to commit to the pre-warm + fallback model variant in an SLA appendix for a pilot?
3) Any objection to a 60-day review clause or do you prefer fixed pilot term language?

I'll prepare a redline SLA (SLA_Draft_v3.pdf) if we align.

—Connor

Attachment: (for internal) SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (will include redline)
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@kitetek.com>

Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for Q3 pilot — capacity expectation and credits

Connor / team — thanks for the swift response and for proposing thoughtful options. We discussed internally and can accept the pilot guardrails you propose with a couple of clarifications: 

- Pilot baseline: 99.90% is acceptable. We need the appendix (pre-warm + fallback) as an operational guarantee (not just guidance).
- Cap and fee: the 20% cap + a one-time 10% provisioning fee is acceptable to procurement provided the fee is applied to month 1 only and is documented in the SOW.
- Review cadence: we prefer a 45-day review (rather than 60) to accelerate ramp decisions.
- Carveouts: KiteTek will accept standard maintenance carveouts but asks for a max 8-hour planned maintenance window per month during pilot (we will provide 72-hour notice).

Please send a redline SLA and a one-page appendix for the operational playbook (pre-warm steps, escalation contacts, fallback model ID). Once received our legal team will do a quick review and loop in procurement for signatures.

Appreciate the willingness to be pragmatic on this.

Sara
